absent: Locking discipline and concurrency guarantees for kernfs nodes open files and attribute callbacks.
Lifetime and reference counting rules for kernfs nodes kobjects and sequence buffers beyond the shown get and put calls.
Namespace matching semantics for directory lookup creation and removal.
Sequence buffer allocation growth and commit behavior and generic seek and mapping fault handling.
Interpretation of visibility callback return values and dynamic binary size callbacks beyond skip invisible and permission masking.
Owner and mode propagation to underlying inodes and permission checking for chmod and chown paths.
Duplicate name warning reporting path and error recovery beyond removal rollback shown.

findings.text: Sequential show for regular attributes acquires a sequence buffer requiring at least one page, clears the page, invokes the type show callback with parent object and attribute, propagates negative status, warns and truncates results at or above page size to page minus one, then commits the length.

Preallocated read requires the supplied buffer to be the open file preallocated area and otherwise warns and returns empty. It calls the type show callback, truncates oversize results to page minus one with diagnostic, drops any prefix before the requested position by shifting the remainder forward, and limits output to the requested length.

Binary read completes empty requests immediately, clips the range to the inode size when sized with end of file at or beyond size, fails when no binary read hook exists, and otherwise delegates to that hook with file parent attribute buffer offset and length.
Regular write completes empty requests with zero and otherwise delegates to the type store callback with parent object attribute buffer and length, returning the callback status.

Binary write clips to inode size when sized and rejects starts at or beyond end, ignores empty requests, fails when no binary write hook exists, and otherwise delegates to that hook with file parent attribute buffer offset and length.

Binary extended operations forward to attribute hooks: mapping delegates directly to the binary mapping hook, seeking prefers the binary seek hook and otherwise uses generic seeking, and open installs a per attribute address mapping when a provider is present.
Notification resolves an optional directory name and then an optional leaf name under the object directory with reference acquisition and release at each step, then signals the final node when found.

Operation tables encode a permission matrix. The empty table has no handlers. Read only exposes sequential display or binary read, write only exposes write, and read write exposes both. Preallocated variants use direct read and mark preallocation. The mapping variant adds binary read and write plus mapping open and seek.

Regular attribute registration fails when type operations are missing, chooses a table from presence of show and store combined with the preallocation request with empty fallback, derives a lock class unless ignored, creates a page sized file using low permission bits with ownership and namespace, warns on duplicate names, and returns creation status.

Binary attribute registration prefers the mapping table when a mapping hook exists, otherwise chooses from read and write presence with empty fallback, derives a lock class unless ignored, creates a file with caller size and low permission bits with ownership and namespace, warns on duplicates, and returns creation status.

Single creation validates object directory and attribute, resolves ownership, and delegates to namespaced mode creation. Batch creation iterates a null terminated array, stops on first error, removes previously added entries in reverse order, and returns the error.
Enabled inline wrappers forward creation and removal to their namespaced forms with a null namespace.
When support is disabled, namespaced creation reports success without action and namespaced removal does nothing.

Group scoped addition and removal resolve a named subgroup with a held reference or hold the object directory directly, then add or remove the named file and release the parent. Addition fails when the subgroup is missing; removal silently skips when the parent is missing.
Permission change locates the leaf by name, merges caller permission bits with existing non permission bits, requests a mode attribute update, releases the leaf, and returns lookup or update status.

Active protection handling pairs acquisition and release. Breaking holds the object then the leaf and suspends protection, releasing the object if the leaf is missing. Unbreaking resumes protection using the leaf parent and then releases leaf and object references.

Removal includes namespaced removal by parent and name, self removal that looks up the leaf warns when absent and reports outcome, iteration over a null terminated array, and binary removal by attribute name.

Name lookup with automatic reference forwards to namespaced lookup with null scope, and removal by name forwards to namespaced removal with null scope. Disabled lookup returns null and disabled removal reports not implemented.
Binary creation validates object directory and attribute, resolves ownership, and delegates to namespaced binary addition using the attribute mode and size.

Ownership change applies user and group updates through an attribute change. Link change validates names and tree presence, resolves the namespaced leaf, checks link type and target identity, then applies the update. File and object changes validate presence with file change requiring a name, and object change also walks default groups of its type.

Group ownership locates the subgroup directory or uses the object directory, applies ownership to the directory then to members. Visibility callbacks can skip zero modes and abort the group on an invisible marker. Missing expected leaves fail the operation.

Formatted output validates that the buffer is present and page aligned and that the start offset lies within the page, formats into the bounded remainder, and returns the produced length, returning zero with warning on invalid input.
Simple binary read copies the requested length from the attribute private area at the given offset into the caller buffer and reports the requested length.

Group file population in update mode first removes each entry, consults visibility callbacks to skip zero modes and clear the invisible flag, warns on and masks permissions to the allowed set, creates regular or binary files with optional dynamic binary size, and on any failure removes all group files before returning.

Group installation skips empty groups, resolves ownership, and derives directory visibility from the first visible member. In update mode a missing directory falls back to creation while a newly invisible group is removed. Otherwise it creates the directory with fixed access permissions when visible and populates files, removing a newly created directory on failure.

Oversize display results, unexpected preallocation buffers, invalid group permissions, misaligned emit buffers, out of range emit offsets, and self removal of absent leaves trigger warnings and are coerced to safe behavior such as truncation masking empty return or failure.

Regular attribute nodes use a page sized allocation while binary nodes use caller supplied size. Creation keeps only low permission bits. Group file permissions are masked to the allowed set plus preallocation flag after warning.

Failures use invalid argument for missing operations or arguments and for type mismatches, missing entry for absent nodes, input output error for missing binary hooks, file too large for writes starting beyond a sized end, and not implemented for disabled removal.
